text:
sarah (pm): Ok team — we need to finalize acceptance criteria & migration scenarios for the v2 route rollout. I sketched a small matrix of customer flows + rollback gates. Please review and call out missing cases.

devin (eng): From runtime POV the biggest risks are: function-calling schema changes and KV cache fragmentation when running v1+v2. We can route by customer header but it increases memory footprint ~1.2x for hot customers.

jules (solutions): Customer scenarios we've seen that must pass: 
- Chat product with long histories (tokens > 8k) where prefix caching matters.
- Tool-calling heavy customers where field names and JSON structure are asserted in downstream code.
- Embeddings consumers that do nearest-neighbor lookups and are sensitive to embedding drift.
Each has different tolerance for "meaningful change".

kai (reliability): Telemetry gating proposal (signals):
- latency: p95 and p99 relative delta vs baseline (thresholds: p95 < +20%, p99 < +25%)
- errors: request error-rate < 0.5% over 24h window
- quality: sample-based regression on customer prompt set (see below)
- drift: embedding cosine drop > X on anchor dataset triggers block
We should automate canary -> metric check -> rollback. ops-bot can trigger if thresholds breach.

mike (customer): FYI our team will not accept >2% quality regression on our canonical prompt set. We need a migration window where both endpoints are viable.

devin (eng): A couple of concrete implementation notes:
- Routing header: `X-Redwood-API-Version: 2` (opt-in).
- Fallback header: `X-Redwood-Fallback: v1` (server side respects for compatibility mode).
- Example shim config we can provide clients:```
# sample shim (node)
fetch(url, {
  headers: {
    'Authorization': 'Bearer ...',
    'X-Redwood-API-Version': '2'
  }
});
```
We should ship SDK helpers to toggle headers per-route.

jules (solutions): For tool-calling: if v2 renames `tool.name` -> `tool_id` we need a compatibility layer that translates incoming v2 shapes to v1 shape for downstream customers, or we clearly document breaking fields and provide a migration script. Most customers prefer a shim.

kai (reliability): Canary plan idea:
- Phase A: internal + Redwood team (48h)
- Phase B: 3 low-risk customers (2 weeks)
- Phase C: 5 mid/large customers (4 weeks) with telemetry + manual signoff
Rollback gates: any of the telemetry signals breach -> automatic rollback and incident alert. ops-bot will post to #release-war-room.

sarah (pm): Proposed acceptance criteria (draft):
1) Embeddings: mean cosine similarity vs baseline anchor set drop < 1.5% and top-K recall loss < 1%
2) Chat (completions): subjective eval on 500 prompt samples: quality regression < 2% (customer-defined pass/fail)
3) Tool calling: all golden tool-call integration tests pass (no schema diffs)
4) Performance: p95 latency increase < 20% and token throughput within 90% of baseline under load
5) Error budget: new-route error-rate <= baseline + 0.2% absolute
If all pass in canary windows, proceed to broader rollout.

devin (eng): Those look good. A couple asks:
- We need a clear definition for "quality regression" (automated eval + human review). Recommend a two-step check: automated scoring (ROUGE/emb-sim/regression model) then 20 human reviews per failing bucket.
- Need dedicated GPU pools for heavy canaries to avoid noisy neighbor effects.

jules (solutions): I'll gather 3 canonical prompt sets per customer: chat, tool-calls, embeddings. Will deliver by EOD Wednesday.

mike (customer): We can share our prompt set but want an NDA addendum for the eval. Also please provide a migration guide we can run in staging.

sarah (pm): NDA note acknowledged — legal will loop in. Migration guide outline (what we'll publish):
- overview + FAQ
- opt-in header and SDK code snippets
- list of known incompatibilities and recommended shims
- automated compatibility test harness (repo)
- rollback and support contact
We should have a short script `redwood-migrate --run-checks` that customers can run against their test prompts.

kai (reliability): Monitoring + alerting checklist for launch:
- traces instrumented per-route/version
- per-customer rate-limited alerts for quality signal breaches
- dashboards: p95/p99, token throughput, error-rate, regression metric
- synthetic jobs: run anchor prompt set hourly during canary
I'll own dashboards and OPS playbook.

devin (eng): Timeline ask from eng: we need 6 weeks to implement routing + shims + SDK helpers + canary infra. If product needs earlier, we must reduce scope (e.g., opt-in only, no automatic fallback).

sarah (pm): Proposed timeline:
- Week 0-2: implement headers + SDK helpers + docs draft
- Week 3-5: implement shims + compatibility tests + canary infra
- Week 6: internal canary -> Phase A
- Week 7-9: Phase B / customer canaries
- Week 10: review + broader rollout decision
Deprecation policy draft: v1 remains supported for new customers for 12 months after v2 GA, full deprecation announced at GA + 12 months, sunset after 24 months with a mandatory migration plan for enterprise customers.

jules (solutions): +1 on timeline but recommend we reserve ability to pause. Also ask legal to prepare a short addendum template for customers sharing prompts.

mike (customer): That timeline works if we get a staging window and the migration script. Also please provide a list of changes that require code edits vs ones we can shim.

sarah (pm): Action items:
- jules: collect canonical prompt sets by Wed (owner)
- devin: estimate engineering tasks & confirm GPU pool needs by EOD Fri
- kai: create dashboards + synthetic jobs baseline by next Tue
- legal/product: NDA addendum template (sarah)
- docs: migration guide skeleton + `redwood-migrate` spec (sarah)
I'll sync with sales on which customers to invite to Phase B.

jules (solutions): Noted. I'll also add a short checklist in the guide: "If you use tool-calling, search for `tool.` fields and run `redwood-migrate --tool-check`"

ops-bot: Canary alert rule created: metric:embedding-drift, threshold:0.015, action:post->#release-war-room.

sarah (pm): Thanks everyone — we'll reconvene after the initial artifacts (prompt sets, eng estimate, dashboards) are in. :eyes: :rocket:

jules (solutions): +1 :thumbsup:

devin (eng): noted. Will flag any scope reductions we need.

kai (reliability): I'll stage the dashboards and post links in the thread when ready.

mike (customer): Appreciate the plan. We'll prep our staging prompts and legal contact.

sarah (pm): Closing out — I'll drop an agenda for the follow-up sync tomorrow.
